extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and working fiction writers (novelists, storytellers, screenwriters)
extracted.subtask_description: A compact, pragmatic craft checklist for fiction writers covering mindset, drafting, sentence-level craft, storytelling fundamentals, character, plot, dialogue, description, revision, and getting published. Draws on Chuck Wendig's informal, blunt guidance to produce testable predicates for evaluating or producing writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Being a Writer
rubrics_metrics.description: Habits, mindset, daily practice that define a working writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes regular writing, reading, and maintaining productive habits; mindset items (persistence, resilience) implied. Use as a meta-dimension for productivity and professional attitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing a Novel
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-form structure, planning, drafting considerations specific to novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers planning vs. discovery, pacing across acts, sustaining character arcs and plot through a long form; evaluate based on coherence, momentum, and structural choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing a Screenplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual storytelling and dialogue practices suitable for screen form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize showing over telling, economy of description, and dialogue that reads as spoken and serves action; consider cinematic beats and scene transitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing a Sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Line-level craft: rhythm, clarity, diction and the 'music' of voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sentence-level variety, cadence, clarity, and how choices support tone and voice; watch for muddled or monotonous sentence rhythms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental narrative principles that make the story work as a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes scene function, pacing, stakes, coherence of narrative question and answer, and the effective use of conflict and subtext across the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character
rubrics_metrics.description: Making people feel real through desires, choices, fears, and losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether characters want things, make decisions, show agency, have consistent voice, and develop across the story; avoid passive characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure, conflict, and momentum that drive narrative events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether plot advances logically, maintains conflict and escalation, and ties back to emotional or thematic stakes; ensure scenes contribute to movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice, subtext, and naturalism in spoken exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue should reveal character and subtext, sound natural without being literal transcription, and serve scene goals; avoid on-the-nose exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensory, restrained, and charged descriptive writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sensory detail that serves mood and character; avoid over-description and clichéd imagery; description should be purposeful and evocative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing/Revising
rubrics_metrics.description: The process of cutting, restructuring, and polishing the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision is the core work: be willing to 'kill your darlings' including structural elements; focus on clarity, pacing, and eliminating redundancies or false cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting Published
rubrics_metrics.description: Querying, submissions, and working with agents/publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice on the mechanics and expectations of the publishing process; evaluate readiness of manuscript, polish of query materials, and understanding of market.

rubrics_metrics.name: You are a storyteller
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary job is to tell stories — prioritize story above gimmick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a foundational test: does the piece function as a story (with stakes, change, and a narrative throughline) rather than an exercise in style or cleverness?

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene utility: threefold purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene must do at least three things: advance plot, reveal character, set tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate scenes against these three functions; scenes that only do one may feel redundant or bloated. Prefer scenes that multitask efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict and subtext
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain conflict on every page and subtext under every line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for explicit and implicit sources of tension; ensure dialogue and action carry underlying motives and unsaid meanings rather than only surface information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid passive characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should not be reactive placeholders; they must act and affect the plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess agency: characters should make choices that cause consequences. Passive characters reduce stakes and reader investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters must make choices — this reveals character and drives plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decision points as moments to reveal values and create cause-effect chains in the narrative; avoid characters who drift without volition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear desires, fears, and loss
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should want things, fear things, and experience loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether desires/fears motivate actions and whether losses produce character change; emotional stakes make conflict meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice as line-level music
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice is the musical quality of prose at the sentence/line level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess consistency and distinctiveness of voice; voice choices should enhance character and tone rather than distract or obscure meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kill your darlings (structural too)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be willing to cut not just lines but scenes, chapters, or arcs that don't serve the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat attachment to favored passages as a hazard; evaluate material by its service to the story, even if beloved by the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cleverness for its own sake
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware the temptation to be clever; aim for writing that is true and surprising rather than merely showy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor honesty and emotional truth; self-conscious cleverness can alienate readers or weaken stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No backstory dumps in chapter 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid large expository backstory dumps at the start of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate backstory gradually and organically; opening should engage with present action and questions rather than pausing for history lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endings must answer the opening question
rubrics_metrics.description: The ending should resolve or answer the question the story raises at the start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether payoff matches setup thematically and emotionally; avoid endings that feel disconnected or merely twisty without resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subvert tropes after mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: Only subvert or play with tropes once you've mastered them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subversion without understanding can come off as novelty; demonstrate competence with conventions before intentionally breaking them.

rubrics_metrics.name: First drafts are allowed to be bad
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept that first drafts will be 'trash' and that perfection is not required initially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as permission to get ideas down; subsequent revision is where craft is applied. Don't stall on first-draft polish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision is the real work
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive improvement happens during revision, not in the initial drafting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize structural edits, pruning, reordering, and rewriting; plan revision passes focused on different levels (plot, scene, sentence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Read constantly
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous reading is essential to craft development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consume widely and critically; use reading to learn techniques, find inspiration, and internalize language patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write daily (but don't moralize)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a regular writing habit without turning it into moral judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage consistency while recognizing life variability; assess productivity by output and progress rather than moralizing about days missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage the internet
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the internet as both a tool and a distraction — actively manage its use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use online resources for research and promotion but limit time-sinks; set boundaries to protect writing time and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Wendig lists as quick-check predicates
rubrics_metrics.description: The lists distill working-novelist craft into short, testable checks that overlap formal craft books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ these items as a concise rubric or revision checklist to rapidly evaluate manuscript health and prioritize edits.
